title: ADU Permits Are Ministerial: 15-Business-Day Completeness, 60-Day Decision
audit_text: An ADU permit application shall be considered and approved ministerially, without discretionary review or a hearing (a)(1). The agency must determine completeness in writing within 15 business days of receipt (a)(2)(A), and approve or deny within 60 days of a complete application when there is an existing dwelling on the lot, or the application is deemed approved (a)(3).
verified_by: HouseMax backend team: read on leginfo. Not reviewed by a licensed permit technician or attorney.
verification_note: Section as amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 520 (SB 543), effective January 1, 2026.

title: ADU Lot Must Be Residentially Zoned With a Proposed or Existing Dwelling
audit_text: The lot is zoned to allow single-family or multifamily residential use and includes a proposed or existing dwelling.
verified_by: HouseMax backend team: read on leginfo. Not reviewed by a licensed permit technician or attorney.
verification_note: Section as amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 67 (AB 1170), effective January 1, 2026.

title: Detached ADU Floor Area Cap (1,200 sq ft) and 4-Foot Side/Rear Setbacks
audit_text: The total floor area for a detached ADU shall not exceed 1,200 square feet (d)(5). A setback of no more than four feet from the side and rear lot lines shall be required for a newly constructed ADU (d)(7). Separately, § 66321(b)(3) bars local rules that would not permit at least an 800 sq ft ADU with four-foot side and rear setbacks.
verified_by: HouseMax backend team: read on leginfo. Not reviewed by a licensed permit technician or attorney.
verification_note: Corrected from the original spec text, which said a 1,200 sq ft ADU 'must be allowed'. § 66314(d)(5) is a cap; the floor the city must allow is 800 sq ft (§ 66321(b)(3), § 66323(a)(2)).

title: Single-Family Lot: One ADU + One JADU, Plus One Detached New-Construction ADU
audit_text: A local agency shall ministerially approve, on a lot with a proposed or existing single-family dwelling, one ADU and one JADU within existing or proposed space (a)(1), and one detached, new-construction ADU with no more than four-foot side and rear setbacks (a)(2), or any combination of these. For the detached unit the agency may limit floor area to not more than 800 sq ft and height per § 66321(b)(4).
verified_by: HouseMax backend team: read on leginfo. Not reviewed by a licensed permit technician or attorney.
verification_note: Section as amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 520 (SB 543), effective January 1, 2026. Multifamily-lot allowances (a)(3)–(4) are not encoded.

title: Cities Must Allow At Least 16 Feet for a Detached ADU
audit_text: A local agency shall not establish a height limit that does not allow at least 16 feet for a detached ADU on a lot with an existing or proposed single-family or multifamily dwelling. This is a floor: a city may allow more.
verified_by: HouseMax backend team: read on leginfo. Not reviewed by a licensed permit technician or attorney.
verification_note: Section as amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 520 (SB 543), effective January 1, 2026.

title: Cities Must Allow At Least 18 Feet for a Detached ADU Near Transit
audit_text: A local agency must allow at least 18 feet for a detached ADU on a lot with an existing or proposed dwelling within one-half mile walking distance of a major transit stop or a high-quality transit corridor (Pub. Res. Code § 21155), plus two additional feet to accommodate a roof pitch aligned with the primary dwelling's roof pitch.
verified_by: HouseMax backend team: read on leginfo. Not reviewed by a licensed permit technician or attorney.
verification_note: The 2-foot roof-pitch allowance is not modeled by the engine (no roof-pitch input).

title: No ADU Parking Standards Within ½ Mile Walking Distance of Public Transit
audit_text: Notwithstanding any other law, a local agency shall not impose any parking standards for an ADU located within one-half of one mile walking distance of public transit. Elsewhere, ADU parking may not exceed one space per unit or per bedroom, whichever is less (§ 66314(d)(10)).
verified_by: HouseMax backend team: read on leginfo. Not reviewed by a licensed permit technician or attorney.
verification_note: Added by Stats. 2024, Ch. 7 (SB 477), effective March 25, 2024. Other exemptions in (a)(2)–(6) (historic district, car share, etc.) are not modeled.

modern_citation: CA Gov. Code § 66329(a); Pub. Res. Code § 30600(a)
title: Coastal-Zone ADUs: Coastal Permit Still Required, Decided in 60 Days Without a Hearing
audit_text: Development in the coastal zone requires a coastal development permit (Pub. Res. Code § 30600(a)). For an ADU, the local government must approve or deny the coastal development permit within 60 days of a complete application, concurrently with the ADU permit, and is not required to hold a public hearing (Gov. Code § 66329(a)).
verified_by: HouseMax backend team: read on leginfo. Not reviewed by a licensed permit technician or attorney.
verification_note: Effective date of the current text was not recorded. Where there is no certified local coastal program, the Coastal Commission decides (§ 66329(b)); not modeled.

title: No Minimum Parking Within ½ Mile of a Major Transit Stop
audit_text: A public agency shall not impose or enforce any minimum automobile parking requirement on a residential, commercial, or other development project located within one-half mile of public transit, defined as a major transit stop (Pub. Res. Code § 21155). The findings-based exception in (b) does not apply to housing projects with fewer than 20 units or at least 20 percent affordable units (c).
verified_by: HouseMax backend team: read on leginfo. Not reviewed by a licensed permit technician or attorney.
verification_note: Added by Stats. 2022, Ch. 459 (AB 2097). For ADUs the engine cites the ADU-specific § 66322(a)(1) instead.
